topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Linear Transformation
sections.content: Define a matrix as a function that transforms a vector. Visually represent a 2D grid being stretched/rotated by a matrix 'A'. Explain that v' = Av.
sections.example: A 2D vector [1, 0] being rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise by matrix A.

sections.title: The Concept of Composition
sections.content: Introduce the idea of applying two transformations sequentially. If transformation A is applied after transformation B, the total effect is a single combined transformation C.
sections.example: A 'Robot Arm' sequence: First, a Rotation matrix (B) turns the arm, then a Scaling matrix (A) extends it.

sections.title: Deriving the Matrix Product
sections.content: Show that the composition (A ∘ B)v = A(Bv). Through substitution, demonstrate that the result is equivalent to (AB)v. Emphasize that the matrix product AB is simply the 'combined instruction manual' for the two transformations.
sections.example: Tracking a cat's movement: Matrix B rotates the cat's coordinate system, and Matrix A flips it; show how AB combines these into one single net-transformation matrix.

sections.title: Visualizing Non-Commutativity
sections.content: Use an animation to show that applying A then B is not the same as B then A. This explains why matrix multiplication AB ≠ BA.
sections.example: A character performing a 'Jump' (Transformation A) then a 'Spin' (Transformation B) results in a different final position than 'Spin' then 'Jump'.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Reiterate that matrix multiplication is not just arithmetic—it is the functional composition of geometric transformations. This provides the foundation for computer graphics and robotics.
sections.example: A 3D video game character: Matrix chains (Bone transformations) determine where the character's hand ends up in space.
